docs.title: ansipath 🌈
docs.text: ansipath makes $PATH legible: each entry is printed on its own line with colors based on directory depth, duplicate entries are highlighted, and dead directories are called out.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• A portable Go binary with no runtime dependencies.
  • Colorized $PATH output and duplicate/dead-path diagnostics.
  • Palette switching stored under $XDG_STATE_HOME/ansipath (or $HOME/.local/state/ansipath).
  • Bash and Zsh pathmunge and which helpers.
  • Shell-init rewriting for .bashrc, .bash_profile, .profile, .zprofile, and .zshrc.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
go build -trimpath -o ansipath .
./ansipath install
ansipath

For a system installation, use sudo ./ansipath install. The installer uses SUDO_USER to update that user’s shell files while installing the binary under /usr/bin.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
ansipath                 # render the current PATH
ansipath --help          # show all commands
ansipath palette list    # list palettes
ansipath palette dracula # select a palette
ansipath remove-dupes    # clean shell-init PATH assignments
ansipath remove-dupes --env

remove-dupes prints an audit trail and asks Undo? N/y; answering y restores the original shell files. To clean the current shell as well, run:

eval "$(ansipath remove-dupes --env)"

The --env form emits sourceable removal commands and ends with an explicit cleaned export. That final export is copied automatically when a supported clipboard utility is available.

docs.title: Ansipath installation
docs.text: ansipath is a single Go binary for Bash and Zsh on Unix-like systems.

docs.title: Build and install
docs.text:
go build -trimpath -o ansipath .
./ansipath install

The default installation writes the binary to $HOME/.local/bin/ansipath, helpers to $HOME/.local/share/ansipath/shell_helpers, and updates only shell init files that already exist. It does not create missing profiles.

For a system prefix while targeting the invoking user’s shell files:

sudo ./ansipath install

When run through sudo, SUDO_USER determines the home directory and shell; the executable is installed under /usr/bin by default. Use --prefix "$HOME/.local" to select another prefix.

docs.title: Palettes
docs.text:
ansipath palette list
ansipath palette dracula

Palette selection is retained in $XDG_STATE_HOME/ansipath/palette, falling back to $HOME/.local/state/ansipath/palette.

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text:
ansipath remove-dupes

This removes duplicate or dead literal path entries from existing shell-init assignments, prints an audit trail, and prompts Undo? N/y. Answer y to restore the original files. To clean the current shell environment too, run:

eval "$(ansipath remove-dupes --env)"

The environment form emits sourceable removal commands and ends with a cleaned export PATH=... line. It copies that final export automatically when a supported clipboard utility is available and does not prompt.
